newsitem.title: UK: LPC-BT to review financing options-banker.
newsitem.headline: LPC-BT to review financing options-banker.

text.p: LONDON, November 4 (LPC) - British Telecom will review its capital markets options to finance the billions of pounds required for its merger with MCI Communications Corp., according to an investment banker close to the company.
"They have tons and tons of options for financing. They have lines with banks, they could use commercial paper and they are enormously cash generative," an investment banker said.

The form of the financing and its size is not yet set, the banker said, but will likely encompass the 2.3 billion stg cash component of the merger, the 2.2 billion stg planned special dividend to existing British Telecom shareholders and potentially cash for share buybacks and investment.
As well, MCI, a much heavier borrower than BT, will have debts of about 2.6 billion stg that will need to be addressed, the banker said.
Gearing of the enlarged group after the merger and special dividend is expected to be around 65 percent, according to British Telecom, as opposed to single digit gearing currently.

The enlarged group will be able to reduce gearing over time, BT said, adding that interest cover will "be very comfortable." Cashflow is large and is more than adequate to cover capital commitments and dividend payments as well as to fund share buybacks, the company added.
There was no doubt among bankers that British Telecom will find plenty of willing lenders.
"No one will come to the conclusion that British Telecom will have any difficulty financing this. It is more a matter of how they want to execute," a commercial banker said.

While British Telecom's financing decision will depend in part on the debt ratings given to the enlarged company, one banker suggested that it may follow the pattern set by AT&T in the US. If so, British Telecom may take a short term funded bank loan to help finance the merger, but is likely to put in place a large commercial paper backstop line from banks.
The majority of its financing needs would then be met through the commercial paper market and through longer term bonds, the banker said.

British Telecom has been an infrequent user of the syndicated loan market. In 1993 it helped to financing its initial investment in MCI through a $500 million short-term syndicated loan arranged by BZW.

MCI recently completed a $2 billion refinancing exercise in the US. That credit was arranged by Bank of Nova Scotia, Chase Investment Bank, Citibank, Mellon Bank and NationsBank. For further details go to LOANS
